answer: Random peer audit stops fake identities. Each agent posts a 20-credit bond at a wharf checkpoint. A random 5% sample is re-run by three peers picked later, so reviewers cannot be bribed. The audit splits each claim like a prism splits light. Making 100 fakes costs 100 x 20 credits, and each sampled fake loses its bond. One honest agent pays one bond, keeps its full reward, and recovers it on passing, with its record stamped by a quartz clock.
